events.title: Opera GX browser released
events.summary: Opera launched Opera GX on June 11, 2019 — a Chromium browser for gamers with [CPU], [RAM], and network limiters plus RGB-themed [UI].
events.about: Opera GX let users cap browser resource usage so games and streams stayed smooth — a niche that grew into millions of installs. It showed Chromium forks could differentiate on UX and vertical features, not just engine speed.

narrative.whyChosen: Opera GX carved out a distinct gamer audience in the Chromium browser market.
narrative.whyImportant: Resource limiters influenced how power users think about browser overhead.
narrative.problemSolved: Gamers and streamers needed a browser that would not hog [RAM] and [CPU] during sessions.

events.title: Kubernetes 1.15 released
events.summary: The [Kubernetes] project released version 1.15 on June 19, 2019 — with CRD pruning, improved scheduling, and continued CSI maturation.
events.about: [Kubernetes] 1.15 refined the extension points operators use — custom resources, admission webhooks, and volume plugins. Each release tightened the control plane teams run in production GKE, EKS, and self-hosted clusters.

narrative.whyChosen: [Kubernetes] 1.15 advanced the CRD and scheduling features platform teams depend on.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed [Kubernetes] evolving from hype to stable infrastructure APIs.
narrative.problemSolved: Cluster operators needed safer upgrades and richer extension mechanisms.
